# Better Auth Gotchas

> Known Better Auth framework patterns that cause silent failures or TypeScript errors. Load all HIGH entries before writing any Better Auth integration code.

## Entries

- [Use better-auth/react for React hooks, not better-auth/client](client-import.md): better-auth/client returns framework-agnostic atoms, not callable React hooks. Import from better-auth/react instead. HIGH.
- [verifyEmail token goes in query param, not top-level body](verify-email-token.md): GET endpoints put params in the query object. Passing token at top level causes a TypeScript error and the call fails. HIGH.
- [Cross-subdomain cookies require explicit config](cross-subdomain-cookies.md): Cookies don't travel between subdomains by default. Must enable crossSubDomainCookies with a leading-dot domain. HIGH.
- [Browser auth client uses import.meta.env not process.env](browser-env-vars.md): process.env does not exist in browser or Cloudflare Pages. Use import.meta.env.VITE_* variables. HIGH.
- [Method names are camelCase from URL paths -- check types](method-names.md): Method names are derived by camelCasing the URL path segments. Guessing from docs is unreliable; check the dist type definitions. MEDIUM.
- [signIn two-factor response: check redirect, not twoFactorRedirect](two-factor-redirect.md): When MFA is enabled, signIn.email returns data.redirect (boolean), not data.twoFactorRedirect. MEDIUM.
- [twoFactor.enable requires the user's current password](two-factor-enable-password.md): Calling twoFactor.enable() without arguments throws TS2554. Must pass { password }. MEDIUM.
- [Organization plugin creates separate tables from custom schema](org-plugin-tables.md): BA's organization() plugin auto-creates its own `organization` + `member` tables. Custom `organizations`/`team_members` tables are a separate system -- frontend writes to BA tables, backend checks custom tables, causing silent FORBIDDEN. HIGH.
- [toNodeHandler + reply.raw bypasses Fastify CORS plugin](fastify-cors-bypass.md): Mounting BA in Fastify via toNodeHandler with reply.raw skips the entire plugin chain. @fastify/cors never runs for auth routes. Must add CORS headers manually. HIGH.
- [setActive() requires organization ID, not slug](set-active-org-id.md): Using slug in setActive causes silent session context loss. Always use the UUID id field. HIGH.
- [Organization plugin doesn't model hierarchical tenancy](organization-plugin-no-hierarchy.md): Plugin is single-level only. For broker -> org -> user or workspace -> team -> user, build the upper layer as a parallel partner_memberships table; do not nest orgs or add parent_organization_id. HIGH.
- [Plugin `after` hook handlers must return an object, not undefined](after-hook-must-return-object.md): runAfterHooks reads result.headers/result.response with no null guard, so a void `return;` throws a TypeError AFTER the endpoint succeeded -- turning a 201 into a 500 with side effects already applied. Return `{}` in every path, or wrap the handler in createAuthMiddleware. HIGH.

- [better-auth generate (Kysely/pg) introspects a LIVE database](generate-needs-live-db.md): generate connects to the configured DB to diff the schema and fails offline with a SASL/connection error; point it at a reachable Postgres or hand-write the schema from the plugin's schema.mjs. MEDIUM.
- [mcp() plugin: mirror /.well-known to root; getMcpSession ignores expiry](mcp-plugin-oauth.md): [DEPRECATED mcp() plugin -- use @better-auth/oauth-provider for new servers] OAuth endpoints live under /api/auth but MCP clients fetch /.well-known/oauth-* at the domain root, and getMcpSession returns expired tokens as valid -- mirror discovery to root and check accessTokenExpiresAt yourself. HIGH.
- [mcp() plugin deprecated -- use @better-auth/oauth-provider for OAuth 2.1 MCP servers](oauth-provider-mcp.md): The built-in mcp() plugin is deprecated in 1.6.x; use the separate @better-auth/oauth-provider + jwt() plugins. Set allowUnauthenticatedClientRegistration for self-registering MCP connectors; verify tokens with issuer=<origin>/api/auth (not the bare origin); serve RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata yourself (resource scopes only, no openid); pin @better-auth/cli on its own (lagging) range; use organizationHooks.afterCreateOrganization (not organizationCreation.afterCreate). HIGH.
- [Custom consent page must echo the signed oauth_query in the POST body](consent-page-oauth-query.md): A custom @better-auth/oauth-provider consentPage must POST `oauth_query` (its full signed URL query) back to /oauth2/consent, or the endpoint returns 400 invalid_request "missing oauth query" and the whole OAuth flow is blocked. The endpoint reads the request from a before-hook keyed on ctx.body?.oauth_query, not from the page URL. HIGH.
- [oauth-provider resource server rejects every token (opaque tokens + wrong JWKS/issuer)](oauth-provider-resource-verification.md): Connector authorizes but every /mcp call 401s ("integration rejected the credentials"). The provider only mints a JWT when the token request sends an RFC 8707 `resource` (default it via a /oauth2/token before-hook), and oauthProviderResourceClient derives jwksUrl/issuer from the bare baseURL (fetches <origin>/jwks 404, expects issuer <origin> not <origin>/api/auth) -- pin jwksUrl + issuer explicitly. HIGH.
- [oauth-provider MCP discovery fails in strict clients: AS metadata issuer mismatch](oauth-provider-strict-client-discovery.md): protected-resource metadata advertises authorization_servers: [<origin>] but the AS issuer is <origin>/api/auth, so strict RFC 8414 clients (Antigravity/Gemini) report "no authorization server metadata found" and show no sign-in button. Advertise <origin>/api/auth and mirror metadata at the path-inserted well-known. HIGH.
- [oauth-provider dynamic client registration returns 200 instead of 201 through Next.js](oauth-provider-dcr-201-status.md): The register handler sets 201 but toNextJsHandler downgrades it to 200 on the wire; strict clients reject DCR with "registration failed with status 200". Intercept POST /oauth2/register and normalize a successful response to 201. HIGH.
- [oauth-provider refresh breaks silent re-auth with RFC 8707 resource binding](oauth-provider-refresh-resource-binding.md): Strict clients (Antigravity) omit `resource` on refresh-token grants, so the provider mints an opaque audience-less token the resource server 401s -- auth silently drops every hour and the client masks it as re-login. Default `resource` via a /oauth2/token before-hook and accept the default audience; offline_access must be in granted scopes for a refresh token to exist at all. HIGH.
